# kroki

Access [kroki](https://kroki.io/) from python.

To install:	`pip install kroki`

Read the overview below, or
view/download/play [this demo notebook](https://github.com/thorwhalen/kroki/blob/main/misc/kroki%20demo.ipynb)
to see how to use this package.

The `kroki` python package is a convenience package for you to be able to generate diagrams,
through [kroki](https://kroki.io/), getting your images as bytes or as ipython objects via python
functions or doing some “cell magic” in your jupyter notebooks.

I suggest you have a look at the [kroki’s excellent homepage](https://kroki.io/)
where you’ll be able to try different diagram types out.
Don’t miss the nice [cheatsheet](https://kroki.io/assets/kroki_cheatsheet_20210515_v1.1_EN.pdf) there.

# Overview

You can get the bytes of an image of a diagram like so:

```python
from kroki import diagram_image_bytes

svn_bytes = diagram_image_bytes("Bob->Alice : Hello!")
# which you can then save in a file...
```

When in a jupyter notebook though, you have a more convenient function that will put those bytes into an IPython display object, which you can then display (will automatically call display if it’s the last command of the cell), amongst other things.

```python
from kroki import diagram_image

diagram_image("Bob->Alice : Hello!")
```

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1906276/211854316-501ec323-bd26-4428-a722-2fa200bfbea3.png)

In both those functions, the default is `diagram_type='plantuml'` and `output_format='svg'`.

But you have other choices.

```python
diagram_image("digraph D {Alice -> Bob, Charles -> Darwin}", diagram_type="graphviz")
```

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1906276/212101184-376b2565-c241-4bcb-81f9-50c1eb538675.png)
```python
png_bytes = diagram_image_bytes("Bob->Alice : Hello!", output_format="png")
png_bytes[:7]
```

```none
b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a'
```

And then, there’s magic, which will allow you to write your diagram source directly in a notebook’s cell.

```python
%load_ext kroki
```

```python
%%kroki

Bob->Alice : Hello!
```

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1906276/211854316-501ec323-bd26-4428-a722-2fa200bfbea3.png)

The default `diagram_type` is still `plantuml`, but you can specify another type if you want.

```python
%%kroki graphviz

digraph D {
    Alice -> Bob, Charles -> Darwin
}
```

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1906276/212101184-376b2565-c241-4bcb-81f9-50c1eb538675.png)

SVG diagrams are shown as an image (`<img src="data:image/svg+xml;...">`) rather than inlined into the page. An inlined SVG’s `<style>` block is page CSS, and mermaid’s would otherwise restyle the notebook’s own output text, e.g. turning it dark gray in dark mode. The raw SVG is still there, as `.data` on the returned object; `kroki.bytes_to_image(svg_bytes, isolate_svg=False)` gives the old inlined display.

The image costs the SVG’s interactivity: no links, no `<title>` tooltips, no text selection, and no web fonts. When you need those and trust the diagram’s CSS, inline it: `%%kroki graphviz --inline` for one cell, or `kroki.ISOLATE_SVG = False` for every diagram in the notebook (then `--isolate` forces the image again). From Python, `kroki.bytes_to_image(svg_bytes, isolate_svg=False)` does the same.

To see what diagram types `kroki` supports through the `diagram_types` variable.

```python
from kroki import diagram_types

print(diagram_types)
```

```none
{'svgbob', 'vega', 'packetdiag', 'mermaid', 'structurizr', 'bytefield', 'vegalite', 'c4plantuml', 'pikchr', 'rackdiag', 'ditaa', 'wavedrom', 'nwdiag', 'graphviz', 'excalidraw', 'plantuml', 'erd', 'umlet', 'actdiag', 'nomnoml', 'bpmn', 'seqdiag', 'blockdiag'}
```

Not all `output_format` values are supported for all diagram types. To which are supported for which types, you can have a look at the `output_formats` dictionary, which which contains both the choices of diagram_type (as keys) and the corresponding output_format each support (as values).

```python
from kroki import output_formats

output_formats["plantuml"]
```

```none
['png', 'svg', 'jpeg', 'base64']
```

```python
output_formats["mermaid"]
```

```none
['svg']
```

```python
output_formats["seqdiag"]
```

```none
['png', 'svg', 'pdf']
```

# Misc

The `kroki` function is just an alias of `diagram_image` which itself, is the composition of `diagram_image_bytes` and `bytes_to_image` to get an iPython image object as your output (which results in displaying the image when it’s the last command of your cell).

The default `diagram_type` of `diagram_image` is `plantuml`.
We also made some ready-to-use `mermaid_image` and `graphviz_image` by fixing `diagram_type` with `functools.partial`.

```python
diagram_image = wrap(diagram_image_bytes, egress=bytes_to_image)
mermaid_image = wrap(
    partial(diagram_image_bytes, diagram_type="mermaid"), egress=bytes_to_image
)
graphviz_image = wrap(
    partial(diagram_image_bytes, diagram_type="graphviz"), egress=bytes_to_image
)
kroki = diagram_image  # alias
```

You can import these directory from `kroki`.

### kroki.ISOLATE_SVG *= True*

Whether SVGs are shown isolated (as an image) when a caller does not say. Set it
to `False` to inline every SVG of a notebook (`kroki.ISOLATE_SVG = False`),
trading the protection of thorwhalen/kroki#1 for interactivity (#7).

### *class* kroki.IsolatedSVG(data=None, url=None, filename=None, metadata=None)

Bases: `SVG`

An IPython `SVG` whose HTML representation cannot restyle the page.

Jupyter frontends (JupyterLab, the classic notebook, VS Code) prefer
`text/html` to `image/svg+xml`, so they show [`svg_to_img_html()`](_autosummary/kroki.html.md#kroki.svg_to_img_html)’s
image instead of inlining the SVG. The raw SVG stays available as `.data`
and as the `image/svg+xml` representation, for exporters that want it.

### *class* kroki.KrokiMagic(shell=None, \*\*kwargs)

Bases: `Magics`

`%%kroki [diagram_type] [output_format] [--inline | --isolate]`.

`--inline` shows an SVG inlined, so its links, tooltips, selectable text and
web fonts work, at the cost of letting its CSS restyle the notebook (#7);
`--isolate` forces the safe image display. Without either, [`ISOLATE_SVG`](_autosummary/kroki.html.md#kroki.ISOLATE_SVG)
decides.

### kroki.bytes_to_image(b, , isolate_svg=None)

A displayable object for diagram bytes: an SVG for SVG bytes, else an Image.

Isolated, an SVG is an [`IsolatedSVG`](_autosummary/kroki.html.md#kroki.IsolatedSVG), shown as an image so its CSS cannot
leak into the notebook. Inlined (`isolate_svg=False`), it is the plain
`IPython.display.SVG`: its CSS reaches the page, but its links, `<title>`
tooltips, selectable text and external fonts work. `None` (the default)
follows [`ISOLATE_SVG`](_autosummary/kroki.html.md#kroki.ISOLATE_SVG).

### kroki.decode_src(encoded_diagram_source)

Decode a diagram source string from a base64 string.

* **Parameters:**
  **encoded_diagram_source** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – The encoded diagram source string.
* **Returns:**
  The decoded string.

```pycon
>>> decode_src('eNpzyk_StXPMyUxOVbBS8EjNyclXBAA7UAXs')
'Bob->Alice : Hello!'
```

### kroki.diagram_image_bytes(diagram_source='Bob->Alice : Hello!', diagram_type='plantuml', output_format='svg')

Get the bytes of a diagram image.

* **Parameters:**
  * **diagram_source** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – The diagram source string.
  * **diagram_type** ([`Literal`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Literal)[`'actdiag'`, `'blockdiag'`, `'bpmn'`, `'bytefield'`, `'c4plantuml'`, `'d2'`, `'dbml'`, `'ditaa'`, `'erd'`, `'excalidraw'`, `'graphviz'`, `'mermaid'`, `'nomnoml'`, `'nwdiag'`, `'packetdiag'`, `'pikchr'`, `'plantuml'`, `'rackdiag'`, `'seqdiag'`, `'structurizr'`, `'svgbob'`, `'symbolator'`, `'tikz'`, `'umlet'`, `'vega'`, `'vegalite'`, `'wavedrom'`, `'wireviz'`]) – The diagram type.
  * **output_format** ([`Literal`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Literal)[`'base64'`, `'jpeg'`, `'pdf'`, `'png'`, `'svg'`, `'txt'`]) – The output format.
* **Returns:**
  The bytes of the diagram image.

### kroki.encode_src(diagram_source)

Encode a diagram source string into a base64 string that can be used in a URL.

* **Parameters:**
  **diagram_source** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – The diagram source string.
* **Returns:**
  The encoded string.

```pycon
>>> encode_src('Bob->Alice : Hello!')
'eNpzyk_StXPMyUxOVbBS8EjNyclXBAA7UAXs'
```

### kroki.svg_to_img_html(svg)

An `<img>` showing *svg* as its own document.

Inlined into a notebook, an SVG’s `<style>` block is page CSS: mermaid’s,
for one, restyles the notebook’s own output text (thorwhalen/kroki#1). As an
image the SVG is a separate document, so its styles (and any script) stay
inside it.

A root `width` that is relative (mermaid writes `100%`) gives the image no
natural width, so the `viewBox` width becomes its `max-width`.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

```pycon
>>> html = svg_to_img_html('<svg viewBox="0 0 120 40" width="100%"><style>p{}</style></svg>')
>>> html.startswith('<img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64,')
True
>>> 'max-width:120px' in html
True
```

# _autosummary/kroki.test.html.md

# kroki.test

Backwards compatible shim for the legacy `kroki.test` module.

The tests themselves now live in `kroki.tests`. They had to move: pytest’s
default `python_files` patterns are `test_*.py` and `*_test.py`, and the
filename `test.py` matches neither, so nothing here was ever collected. The
assertions ran only because `--doctest-modules` imports every module under
`testpaths` and this one called its own test function at import time – meaning a
regression showed up as a collection error that aborted the entire run, rather than
as one failing test.

This module is kept so that `from kroki.test import test_code_codecs` keeps
working. It re-exports from `kroki.tests.test_codecs`, which does not import
pytest, so importing `kroki.test` still requires nothing beyond `kroki` itself.

### Functions

| `test_code_codecs`()   |    |
|------------------------|----|
